verses.author: model_A
verses.text: The train slows for a station no one gets off at.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone's phone still lit, face-down
on the empty seat, glowing
for no one to answer.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Rain starts on the far platform first,
then finds the near one too --
same sky, different waiting.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I keep checking the window for my own reflection --
the glass gives me the platform instead,
someone else's umbrella opening where my face should be.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The umbrella folds shut, walks away --
and still I stand here,
borrowing its shape for a face.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The train doors chime twice before closing --
once for the ones who board,
once for the ones who only meant to.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The platform empties like a held breath let go --
I'm still deciding
which kind of leaving this was.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The clock above the tracks skips a minute --
no one else seems to notice
that we've all arrived somewhere without moving.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The vending machine hums the same three notes --
I feed it a coin
for something I already know I don't want.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The pigeons scatter when no train is coming --
they know something about waiting
I haven't learned yet.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A paper cup rolls to the yellow line and stops --
even the wind
knows where it isn't allowed to go.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone's left umbrella dries in the rafters --
it gave up on rain
long before the rest of us did.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The clock above the platform runs three minutes fast --
just enough
for hope to catch what's already left.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The vending machine hums its one long note --
nobody feeds it coins anymore,
but it keeps the pilot light of waiting lit.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A pigeon studies the departures board --
it can't read a word of it,
yet somehow always knows when to fly.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The lost-and-found box grows heavier each season --
gloves without hands,
still shaped like reaching.
